summary.title: Let's Build a Compiler (in Haskell)
summary.one_liner: A blog series that works through Jack Crenshaw's "Let's Build a Compiler" tutorial by reimplementing its hands-on compiler project in Haskell.
takeaways: Crenshaw's LBaC is a hands-on, top-down introduction to building a compiler, as an alternative to the Dragon Book.
This series reworks LBaC's original Turbo Pascal project in Haskell.
The author fills in theory and alternatives that LBaC skims over.
Code and articles are published on GitHub; the LBaC PDF and Haskell Platform are needed to follow along.
Posts are irregular, written in spare time.
summary.summary: The author introduces a series of articles that follows Jack Crenshaw's Let's Build a Compiler (LBAC) tutorial, rewriting its compiler project in Haskell instead of the original Turbo Pascal 4.0. The page explains why LBaC was chosen (a practical, top-down approach with quick results) and why Haskell was picked (its tooling for parsers, lexers and LLVM, and its difference from everyday languages). Readers are told to follow along with the experiments, using the GitHub code, the LBaC PDF and the Haskell Platform. The page is an intro post, so no compiler code is covered yet.
